capabilities: Capture definitions, results and relations as draft records citing source lines and verbatim quotes
Bind relation and node roles from per-base document types with user-defined kinds
Search records across all registered bases with fused lexical, dense-embedding and name lanes
Look up text selections and view a record's typed neighbourhood in a lookup sidebar
Review and accept drafts, and let agents capture, compile and query via Skills and an MCP server
extras: Desktop only (does not load on mobile); requires Obsidian 1.13.7 or newer. Conflicts with the Hidden Folders Access plugin, which it detects and disables its own indexing for. Agent web/paper search sends data to Exa, Wikipedia and arXiv; embedding models (about 2.3 GB) download from the Hugging Face Hub.
motivation: The author believes research sources reduce to a few knowledge nodes, so a knowledge graph should be the foundation and retrieval should depend on it rather than whole documents.
problem: Obsidian has no structured knowledge base where research facts and relations cite exact source paths, line ranges and verbatim quotes, retrievable across vaults by semantic search.

relations.evidence: Link its own runtime: kgd claude link then kgd claude doctor, or kgd codex link
kgd claude link|doctor, kgd codex link|doctor | Install or verify the Skills
OMP loads stdio MCP servers natively from .mcp.json, .omp/mcp.json or ~/.omp/agent/mcp.json
web and paper searches go to Exa (mcp.exa.ai)

requires.name: kgd CLI (Python core installed via uv)
model provider key for the optional agent

summary: Local research knowledge base that stores definitions, results and typed relations as Markdown records citing source lines, with fused lexical and semantic search.
